items.title: the entry-shaped REPLAY pin (`replay_differential::an_entry_shaped_world_agrees_between_replayed_and_rederived_module_checks`) required EVERY warm pair to reuse while the base cache's 8 MiB LRU budget (`BASE_CACHE_DEFAULT_BUDGET`, ~28–30 worlds at ~280 KiB) EVICTS a slow pair's world under sixteen workers before its second analysis — flaky on the Order 40 seal already (`element-syntax.vl`), 2 of 3 at idle on 9bc243d9 (`list-cell.vl`; four more corpus programs + ~1,000 std lines took the retained count 30–32 → 28–29), red on CI's ubuntu-1 and windows-1. FIXED test-side (bisect-41 50d38921): the pin lifts the budget to unlimited for its two legs and restores it (+410 MiB peak RSS for ~20 s). The honest alternative: require exact reuse only for pairs that actually HIT the cache plus a ≥ 90 % hit rate (so the pin cannot pass on nothing) — needs a per-thread 'served from cache' signal the analyzer does not have; and the file's header (lines 92–95) still says the binary holds ONE test (it holds two, both flipping the global `set_world_reuse` under plain `cargo test`)
items.discussion: the Order 41 seal (2026-09-25); the bisect lane's report; with N129/N131 (the plain-cargo-test races)
items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-09-25 (the Order 41 seal; the bisect lane's report)
items.body: Options: (a) keep the test-side budget lift (shipped; +410 MiB during the pin); (b) the honest pin — exact reuse only for pairs that HIT the cache + a ≥ 90 % hit-rate floor, which needs the analyzer to report 'served from cache' per thread; (c) raise `BASE_CACHE_DEFAULT_BUDGET` for everyone (a product change — the LSP's memory). Rec (b) when the signal is cheap; fix the file header either way.
